restatements.text: Provides the title of the act as the Improving Transparency, Effectiveness, and Efficiency in California Government Act of 2026.
Lists findings and declarations regarding the cost of living, taxation levels, spending on public programs, and the state spending limit.

States the purpose of the act is to require the California State Auditor to conduct upfront and ongoing audits of state programs funded by new or higher special taxes, share results with the public, and prohibit exemptions from the state spending limit.

Requires the California State Auditor to prepare a pre-election financial and performance audit for any proposed special tax initiative, covering efficiency, fraud, goal achievement, and cost-saving recommendations. Copies must be provided to state officials, posted online, and summarized in the state voter information guide. The Auditor is reimbursed from the tax revenue if the measure passes.

Mandates the State Auditor to conduct ongoing financial and performance audits every four years for all programs receiving money from special taxes enacted on or after January 1, 2026, and to invite input from the public and the Legislative Analyst's Office.
Prohibits any state tax enacted on or after January 1, 2026, from being exempted or excluded from the Government Spending Limitation.
Defines terms used in the article, including special tax, special tax initiative, and exempted or excluded from the Government Spending Limitation.
Applies the new article to all statewide initiative measures submitted to voters on or after January 1, 2026.

Declares that this measure conflicts with any other initiative on the same ballot that imposes different audit rules on special taxes or exempts a state tax from the Government Spending Limitation, providing that this measure prevails if it receives more affirmative votes.
Contains a severability clause ensuring that if any part of the act is found invalid, the rest remains in effect.
Specifies that the act takes effect and becomes operative at the earliest possible date allowed by the California Constitution.
Instructs that the act be liberally construed to give effect to its intent.

Requires the Attorney General to appoint independent counsel to defend the act if the Governor and Attorney General refuse to do so, and creates a continuous appropriation from the General Fund to cover the costs.

evidence.quote: No state tax that is enacted or takes effect on or after January 1, 2026 shall be exempted or excluded from the Government Spending Limitation.
evidence.why: The measure limits state spending authority by prohibiting exemptions to the Government Spending Limitation for any state tax enacted after 2025.

evidence.quote: the California State Auditor shall commence with the preparation of a pre-election financial and performance audit of each of the program(s) that would receive moneys from the special tax.
evidence.why: The measure expands government mandates by requiring the California State Auditor to conduct a new type of pre-election audit.

evidence.quote: Copies of the pre-election financial and performance audit shall be delivered to the Governor, the Legislature, and the Secretary of State, and shall be posted on the California State Auditor’s website and made available to the public.
evidence.why: The measure increases transparency by requiring pre-election audits of programs tied to special taxes to be posted publicly online.

evidence.quote: the executive summary from the pre-election financial and performance audit shall be printed in the state voter information guide immediately following the impartial analysis prepared by the Legislative Analyst.
evidence.why: The measure enhances transparency by mandating that a summary of the audit findings be included directly in the state voter guide.

evidence.quote: For all special taxes enacted by the Legislature or by a statewide initiative measure on or after January 1, 2026, the California State Auditor shall conduct ongoing financial and performance audits of each program that receives moneys from the special tax.
evidence.why: The measure strengthens oversight by requiring regular performance and financial audits for all programs receiving new special taxes.

evidence.quote: a continuous appropriation is hereby made from the General Fund to the Controller, without regard to fiscal years, in an amount necessary to cover the costs of retaining independent counsel to faithfully and vigorously defend this Act
evidence.why: The measure guarantees continuous funding from the General Fund to pay for independent counsel to defend the law.

evidence.quote: No state tax that is enacted or takes effect on or after January 1, 2026 shall be exempted or excluded from the Government Spending Limitation.
evidence.why: The measure limits budget flexibility by locking in a spending cap, prohibiting any new state tax from being exempted from the Government Spending Limitation.

evidence.quote: a continuous appropriation is hereby made from the General Fund to the Controller, without regard to fiscal years, in an amount necessary to cover the costs of retaining independent counsel to faithfully and vigorously defend this Act
evidence.why: The measure locks in mandatory spending by establishing a continuous appropriation for legal defense that operates without regard to fiscal years.

evidence.quote: No state tax that is enacted or takes effect on or after January 1, 2026 shall be exempted or excluded from the Government Spending Limitation.
evidence.why: The measure restricts state spending authority by prohibiting exemptions from the Government Spending Limitation for new state taxes.

evidence.quote: the California State Auditor shall commence with the preparation of a pre-election financial and performance audit of each of the program(s) that would receive moneys from the special tax.
evidence.why: The measure expands the mandates of the California State Auditor by requiring it to conduct new pre-election audits.

evidence.quote: For all special taxes enacted by the Legislature or by a statewide initiative measure on or after January 1, 2026, the California State Auditor shall conduct ongoing financial and performance audits of each program that receives moneys from the special tax.
evidence.why: The measure increases checks and balances by requiring the independent State Auditor to regularly review the performance and finances of programs funded by new special taxes.

analysis.answer: Current law was not provided. The measure introduces mandatory pre-election audits for proposed special taxes, ensures these findings are published in the voter guide, mandates ongoing audits for enacted special taxes, and prevents exemptions from the state spending limit for new taxes.

The measure creates direct costs for the State Auditor to conduct extensive financial and performance audits. If a tax measure passes, audit costs are reimbursed from its revenue; if it fails, the pre-election audit costs appear to remain an expense of the state's General Fund. Opportunity costs include potential restrictions on overall state spending capacity due to the strict enforcement of the spending limit.

Programs receiving new special tax funds pay for the successful pre-election and ongoing audits out of their new revenues. Taxpayers and voters benefit from increased access to information in voter guides and public reports regarding program efficiency and spending.

Proponents of new special taxes might face higher hurdles to passing initiatives due to the publication of potentially critical audit findings in the voter guide, such as identifying waste or recommending significant budget cuts. The state legislature will face tighter constraints on funding new programs because it can no longer exempt new taxes from the Gann Limit.

The text addresses perceived government waste, program inefficiency, and taxation that bypasses the state spending limit. Its mechanism of mandatory audits provides transparency but relies on voters and policymakers to act on the findings to realize savings. The prohibition on exemptions directly blocks a method previously used to allow spending of tax revenues above the state cap.

The California State Auditor gains considerable discretion and influence by evaluating program performance, assessing what constitutes waste or fraud, and making official recommendations for budget savings that are presented directly to voters.

A portion of any new special tax revenue will be directly diverted to reimburse the State Auditor for the reasonable costs incurred during pre-election and ongoing audits, slightly reducing the funds available for the actual program.
Because this measure adds a new article to the California Constitution, it would require another statewide ballot initiative approved by voters to be undone or significantly altered.

flags.quote: Notwithstanding anything to the contrary contained in Chapter 6 (commencing with Section 12500) of Part 2 of Division 3 of Title 2 of the Government Code or any other law, the Attorney General shall appoint independent counsel
flags.note: Overrides existing laws to mandate the appointment of independent counsel if state officials refuse to defend the act.

flags.quote: If the special tax initiative is approved by voters, the California State Auditor shall be reimbursed from the revenue generated by the special tax initiative for reasonable costs incurred in preparing the pre-election financial and performance audit, as determined by the Controller.
flags.note: The measure mandates the State Auditor to complete pre-election audits for proposed initiatives, but only provides a funding source for reimbursement if the initiative is approved, potentially leaving the costs unfunded if it fails.

flags.quote: The provisions of this Act are severable.
This Act shall take effect at the earliest possible date in accordance with Section 10 of Article II of the California Constitution. This Act shall become operative on the same day it takes effect.
flags.note: Specifies that the act takes effect and becomes operative immediately upon the earliest possible date allowed by law.

flags.quote: to require the California State Auditor to conduct upfront and ongoing audits of all state programs that are targeted to receive revenue from new or higher special taxes... while also prohibiting exemptions from the state spending limit
flags.note: Bundles comprehensive auditing and reporting requirements for special taxes with a blanket constitutional prohibition on exempting any new state taxes from the state spending limit.
